title: Public Hearing on the draft RTS on the conditions for the functioning of AML/CFT supervisory colleges in the financial sector

paras.text: Public input on these draft Regulatory Technical Standards is essential to ensure that AML/CFT supervisory colleges operate consistently and effectively across the Union.

This draft RTS establishes conditions for conditions for the functioning of AML/CFT colleges in the financial sector. Accordingly, the draft RTS preserves continuity with supervisory practices that have proven effective by retaining the core elements under the framework set out in the Joint Guidelines on cooperation and information exchange between competent authorities supervising credit and financial institutions under the Directive (EU) 2015/849, issued by the European Supervisory Authorities in December 2019.
Having clear, harmonised and legally binding rules governing the organisation and functioning of AML/CFT supervisory colleges is a fundamental step to promote supervisory cooperation.

Evidence gathered to date suggests that, while AML/CFT colleges in the financial sector have made a positive contribution to supervisory cooperation, this framework can be further improved. In particular, findings identified by the European Banking Authority in its Report on the functioning of AML/CFT colleges in 2024/2025, together with observations drawn from AMLA’s participation in AML/CFT college meetings since November 2025, indicate that colleges’ effectiveness could be further enhanced through stronger risk-based cooperation and more structured discussions on the need for coordinated supervisory approaches.
